description:
Record the purchase terms and arrange the payment needed to complete checkout. This call never submits the order.

For a checkout you will submit, call with `status: draft` before asking the main agent to review the cart through `browser.request_input`. Give the purchase description and terms in `summary`, and its payment amounts as the page shows them. Draft records the details without requesting payment approval. A call with purchase details and no `status` is also a draft, and a draft replaces any earlier ready terms, so `checkout.submit` refuses until a later call with `status: ready`. Resolve Muse's requested changes before calling with `status: ready`, which obtains any required payment approval and prepares the selected payment method. An empty card form can be ready when a card is available to enter or preparation will supply one. Set `record_only: true` to record facts without arranging payment.

Set `payment_route` to `wallet` for secure payment through Muse Wallet, `merchant_saved` for a payment method already stored by this merchant that the user chose, or `takeover` to prepare the checkout for the user to complete. For takeover, the call records terms and returns immediately. Continue through the available checkout steps, then report `needs_input` with `reason: payment` when the user must act. Include the prepared cart and remaining steps in the report. Describe an offered merchant-saved method in `saved_card`. For `wallet`, the runtime opens payment approval automatically. Use `takeover` when the requested method cannot be supplied by the runtime, such as PayPal, or the checkout has no supported wallet path. Preserve that method in the final handoff. Omit the route only when no payment method is required or while gathering facts.

To see the available wallets without changing the recorded purchase, supply only `tab`.

Finish with `browser.report`, which records the final outcome. To record an outcome while continuing, supply `outcome`, its evidence in `summary`, and any merchant `confirmation`. Before submitting again after a confirmed failure, record `outcome: not_placed`. Include changed purchase terms, or omit purchase inputs for an outcome-only update.

Keep the purchase terms current as checkout progresses. Your checkout instructions say which changes need a fresh Muse review. Payment approval and funding are reused when they still cover the purchase. When a virtual credit card is returned, use its number, expiry, CVC and any provided billing address to fill out the checkout form with `browser.act`, just as you would with any credit card. Use `checkout.submit` at the final order step.

status.description: Use draft while gathering terms, or ready to request payment after the main agent has confirmed the cart. For takeover, ready only records terms and leaves completion to the user. An empty card form can be ready when a card is available to enter or preparation will supply one. Omission records a draft; a call with only tab reads wallet availability. A draft replaces earlier ready terms, and checkout.submit needs ready ones.

record_only.description: Record the purchase without requesting payment. Defaults to false.

summary.description: Describe the purchase, its terms and any open questions, including contents, options, delivery, account details and commitments. When recording an outcome, explain what the merchant shows.

merchant_name.description: The merchant name shown on the page. Omit when not shown.

line_item_names.description: Names of the purchased items for Link. Shop Pay can supply these through line_items.

final_amount.description: Amount due now as a plain number in the checkout's currency, as the page shows it, without digit-grouping separators and with . as the decimal point: 1234.56 for USD 1,234.56 or 1.234,56 €, 19800 for JPY 19,800, 12.345 for KWD 12.345. Keep additional conditional charges separate.

currency.description: Three-letter ISO currency code, such as USD.

conditional_amount.description: Maximum additional conditional charge for the whole purchase, as a plain number in the same currency, formatted like final_amount. Explain the conditions in summary. Omit when none applies.

payment_route.description: Use wallet for secure payment through Muse Wallet. When a virtual credit card is returned, use its number, expiry, CVC and any provided billing address to fill out the checkout form, just as you would with any credit card. Use merchant_saved for a payment method already stored by this merchant that the user chose, or takeover to prepare checkout as far as possible and leave completion to the user. Takeover returns immediately without payment approval or submission; report the remaining steps when the user must act. Omit only while gathering facts or when no payment method is required.

payment_method.description: The page's wording, including any explanation that this does not apply. Omit when not shown.

payment_credential_valid_for_seconds.description: Requested Link card lifetime after approval, in seconds; null uses the default. Keep the same duration unless payment timing changes.

merchant_country.description: For Shop Pay, the merchant's two-letter country code.

line_items.description: For Shop Pay. Supply each line's name, quantity and a unit price or line total before requesting payment. Prices are plain numbers in the checkout's currency, as the page shows them, like final_amount.

shipping_address.description: For Shop Pay. A partial address can be recorded while gathering terms; complete it before requesting payment.

outcome.description: What the merchant shows about the order. Explain the evidence in summary.

confirmation.description: The merchant's order or booking confirmation, including its identifier when shown.
